{{short description|American mathematician}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=July 2025}}
'''Daniel Leonard Ocone''' (born 1953) is a Professor in the Mathematics Department at [[Rutgers University]], where he specializes in [[probability theory]] and [[stochastic process]]es.<ref>Source: Rutgers University web site</ref> He obtained his Ph.D. at [[MIT]] in 1980 under the supervision of [[Sanjoy K. Mitter]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy |id=47879 }}</ref>  He is known for the [[Clark–Ocone theorem]] in [[stochastic analysis]].  The continuous Ocone martingale is also named after him; it is a continuous [[martingale (probability theory)|martingale]] that is conditionally Gaussian, given its [[quadratic variation]] process.<ref>Van Zanten: Continuous Ocone martingales as weak limits of rescaled martigales, Elec Comm Probability, 7(2002) 205-212 [http://www.emis.de/journals/EJP-ECP/_ejpecp/ECP/include/getdocdb48.pdf]</ref>
